text: A nightly pipeline fails at 2 a.m. with a KeyError, fifteen minutes before the morning dashboards are due — a real-shaped failure that pulls together the whole chapter.
Before pasting anything in, the engineer strips the log of identifying data. The assistant drafts a plausible hypothesis about a new nullable column with no default.
The engineer doesn't ship the hypothesis. They query the actual source table and confirm it — that confirmation against real data is what makes it a finding.
Copilot drafts the one-line fix instantly. The engineer re-runs it against the failing rows and confirms the output matches the actual business rule.
The AI sped up every draft; a human made every call about what was actually true. Next up: AI in the production practices from Course 3.
